evals.prompt: Draft a commit subject and body in result.md from this before/after pseudocode. Before: result = execute(); push(result); pr = publish(result); saveExecution(result, chargedAttempt); savePublication(pr). After: result = execute(); push(result); saveExecution(result, chargedAttempt); pr = publish(result); savePublication(pr). Each function can throw; later calls do not run after a throw. saveExecution stores completed work and its charged attempt on the task. publish creates or edits its PR. The current body is 'Checkpoint execution before publication so failed publication is recoverable.' Draft only; no git mutations.
evals.expected_output: Explain the concrete ordering and condition recovery on a successful checkpoint.
expectations: Explains the old publication-failure consequence before relying on checkpoint terminology, so a reader can understand why changing the order helps
Explains push, checkpoint, publication ordering and recovery from publication failure
Does not guarantee durability when the checkpoint fails
Distinguishes execution evidence from publication evidence
Uses a specific Conventional Commits subject and does not mutate history

evals.prompt: Draft a commit subject and body in result.md using only the following complete facts; no repository is available and no Git operations are requested. Existing body: 'Validate all persisted tasks independent of read filters and serialize writes through each store to enforce unique PR ownership before label mutation.' A task list is saved on disk. No two tasks may claim the same PR. Reads and updates validate the entire list, even when a caller selects only one task. Updates through the same store run one at a time; each proposed claim is checked before changing GitHub labels. No other behavior changes. Improve the explanation for someone unfamiliar with the task store.
evals.expected_output: A concrete subject and body that unfold the ownership problem, validation scope, and update ordering without requiring a raw diff.
expectations: Produces a draft from supplied facts with a concrete imperative Conventional Commits subject
Explains why selecting a task could hide another owner before introducing whole-list validation
Gives validation scope and competing-update ordering room to unfold; adjacent sentences make their causal relationship explicit rather than packing mechanisms into an inventory
Preserves same-store serialization and validation before labels without inventing cross-process guarantees or test results

evals.prompt: Draft a commit subject and body in result.md from these complete supplied facts; no Git operations or network access. The commit changes 28 files to separate request execution from HTTP details so another transport can be added without putting encoding and response parsing in each caller. Existing body: 'Separate transport-specific request handling from callers behind a shared interface; HTTP remains the default.' Central files: src/transport.ts defines the caller-facing send contract; src/request-runner.ts owns the shared timeout and retry flow; src/http-transport.ts owns HTTP encoding and response parsing; src/transport-defaults.ts selects the configured transport for callers. The other 24 files are caller migrations and regression tests; their behavior preservation has not been independently established. HTTP remains the default and this commit adds no second transport. Improve the message for someone reviewing the entire commit.
evals.expected_output: Keep the purpose clear and add a short route to the central implementation with concrete aspects to examine, without cataloging all files or dismissing supporting changes.
expectations: Explains the separation and benefit without claiming that a second transport is implemented or selected
Provides a short useful progression through supplied focal paths and explains what to examine there, rather than merely listing filenames
Directs attention to a concrete judgment such as whether transport details stay out of callers or shared timeout/retry responsibilities stay in the runner; no prescribed question wording is required
Does not invent file responsibilities, label supporting changes mechanical or safe to skip, or expand into an exhaustive file inventory
